Each employee is paid for six hours, of which exactly eighty percent is available for these jobs. All jobs are available at the start, can be freely assigned, and have only an end-of-day deadline. Each job must be completed by one person, no overtime or queueing buffer is allowed, and productive time per person fits a whole number of jobs. What is the minimum required headcount, as a whole number of people?

follow_up.question: What operational buffer does the minimum headcount omit?
follow_up.reference: It omits queueing targets, uncertain arrivals, sickness and other variability beyond the stated productive-time allowance. A practical staffing recommendation should test those service requirements before using this arithmetic minimum.
